Frontier AI performance at half the price. That is not a rumor — it shipped this week.

Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5, scoring within 0.5% of the leading competitor on Cursor Bench 3.2, hitting a perfect score on IMO 2026, and pricing it at $5 per million input tokens. That is exactly 50% less than what the top alternative charges for comparable capability.

More important than the price cut is what Anthropic optimized for. Opus 5 is designed for longer, more reliable agentic work — lower latency, reduced token consumption, and significantly less human babysitting to complete real tasks. This is a direct play for enterprise deployment at scale.

The frontier AI market is now clearly splitting. One camp competes on peak intelligence at premium cost. The other competes on reliable task completion at a price point that makes large-scale deployment viable. For most enterprise workflows, the second proposition is substantially more valuable.

The practical takeaway for leadership teams: cost per completed task is now the metric to track. Not benchmark rankings. Not parameter counts. How much does it cost to get real work done reliably with minimal human oversight?

When frontier performance drops to half the cost it was last quarter, the bottleneck shifts from technology to organizational readiness.
